title: Whole Grain Pasta with Cream Sauce, Seafood and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: This dish features whole‑grain pasta tossed in a smooth cream sauce, combined with seafood (shrimp, mussels, calamari) and a mix of vegetables (broccoli, carrot, bell pepper). Whole‑grain pasta retains more fiber and nutrients than refined white pasta.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole‑grain pasta provides more fiber, B‑vitamins and minerals than traditional refined pasta.
The cream sauce is often made with cream and Parmesan, giving the dish a velvety texture.
Seafood such as shrimp and mussels are rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for heart health.
Adding vegetables boosts antioxidant content and vitamins C and A.
The combination of seafood and fresh vegetables is a staple of Mediterranean cuisine, known for its health benefits.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain pasta supports digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Seafood supplies essential polyunsaturated fats that support heart and brain function.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Vegetables add vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium, while whole grain contributes magnesium and iron.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The combination of pasta and seafood provides a complete set of amino acids.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Whole‑grain pasta raises blood sugar more slowly than white pasta.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels or calamari.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Cream sauce adds saturated fat and calories; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Prepared sauces often contain salt; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Food interactions
items.content: Omega‑3 can enhance the effect of anticoagulants; consult a doctor if you take such medication.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, mixed with the cream sauce, seafood and vegetables. Finish with fresh basil, a squeeze of lemon, or grated Parmesan to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry whole‑grain pasta in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked leftovers should be kept in the refrigerator for up to 2 days and reheated before serving.
